plain: An income statement typically includes revenue (total sales generated), cost of goods sold (direct costs of producing what was sold), and gross profit (revenue minus COGS). Below that come operating expenses like salaries, rent, marketing, and R&D, which get subtracted to find operating income. Then non-operating items like interest expense and taxes are factored in to arrive at net income, the final "bottom line" figure. Many statements also break out earnings per share (EPS) and may separate operating income from one-time or unusual items to give a clearer picture of core business performance. Together these elements show how much money a company made, spent, and kept over a specific period.
